# Native capability fixtures

The machine-readable [format fixture manifest](manifest.json) is the source of
fixture IDs, repository-relative delivery paths, byte counts, SHA-256 hashes,
origins, licenses, dependencies, geometric expectations and intended outcomes
for the conformance fixtures. Their authors must register each new fixture and
its exact file path with the capability ledger owner before implementation.
Verify the manifest's byte counts and digests against the staged payload before
using a fixture as evidence; this document does not certify a test run.

The lifecycle spec has a separate, independently authored in-memory fixture:

| Fixture | Source and license | Expected behavior | Size and identity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lifecycle-triangle.glb` | Generated by `triangleGlb()` in [`native-capability-lifecycle.spec.ts`](../../browser/native-capability-lifecycle.spec.ts); authored for Aura3D under the repository's MIT license using the glTF 2.0 format | One red unlit triangle on black. The typed model path loads it, survives resize and explicit remount after context recovery, and releases its resources. | 624 bytes; SHA-256 `82790c47fc6a0be1965462b2b4ba5f87d8208167722a45dddfabd69d01747f13` |

The browser spec serves these bytes only at its intercepted same-origin
`/fixtures/native-capabilities/lifecycle-triangle.glb` URL. It verifies the
size and digest before serving. It is a geometric test subject, not a
production asset or a statement of browser/device support.

The pixel unit tests independently generate small RGBA arrays in memory: solid
transparent, black and white frames; black frames with isolated red noise or a
red subject; a deliberately dark subject; and a gray background with balanced
black and white outliers. They are test-generated values, not image assets.
